planting.note: This is a short-day plant, so uninterrupted nights of 14+ hours of darkness are required to trigger reblooming after the first flush fades.

directions: Grow in bright, indirect light indoors or morning sun outdoors, letting the succulent leaves dry out fully between waterings. This series produces small, tightly packed rosette-form double blooms that resemble miniature roses across a wide range of named color strains. Keep plants compact by pinching spent flower stalks after the main bloom flush. To force rebloom, give the plant roughly six weeks of 14-hour uninterrupted darkness followed by cool nights.

directions: This Danish-bred 1989 cultivar was selected for its smaller leaves, heavier bud count, and notably quicker finish time than older florist kalanchoes of its era, and it later became a reference standard against which newer patented cultivars were judged. Grow it in a bright windowsill or under strong indirect light, watering only once the succulent leaves feel slightly soft. Deadhead spent red flower clusters to keep the tidy, dense habit and encourage secondary branching.

directions: This series was bred specifically to shrug off summer heat outdoors, holding up to only weekly watering while staying naturally resistant to powdery mildew. Plants form a well-branched, ball-shaped mound smothered in small single blooms in shades ranging from crimson and violet to bicolor pink-and-white and bright orange. Site containers where they get strong sun and good airflow, and let the soil dry between waterings to keep the roots healthy through hot stretches.

common_name: Deck'd Out Kalanchoe (Large-Container Garden Florist Kalanchoe)

planting.note: This is a short-day plant, so uninterrupted nights of 14+ hours of darkness are required to trigger reblooming after the first flush fades.

directions: Bred for sheer size, this series is meant to fill a large patio pot rather than a small windowsill, growing noticeably bigger and more vigorous than typical florist kalanchoes. It flowers continuously through the warm season in shades like premium pink, radiant rose, magenta, and a coral bicolor, drawing bees and other pollinators to the deck or patio. Give it a large container with fast-draining mix, full sun, and only occasional deep watering, since the thick leaves store plenty of moisture on their own.
